title: Require two directions above height 64 in three-query cubic repair at r=15
body:
## Summary

**Finite certificate with a scoped algebraic proof.** Every exact three-query dyadic repair of the fixed cubic reader at arity 15 needs at least two source directions whose primitive integer coefficient height exceeds 64. The third direction is unrestricted. Source changes act on the two arbitrary dirty sources, all fifteen original children remain, and both sources must be restored.

```text
two primitive directions of height at most 64
  -> only possible third direction, with no height cutoff
  -> unique forced weights
  -> no admissible dyadic triple in 12,698,280 pairs
```

Only `research/cubic-r15-height-obstruction/` is added. The result was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit apoursh's #7475 remaining-arity question, #6212 general-frame contract and lower bound, #6215 pure-B obstruction, and Nick Petalas's #6200 reader/defect and #6653 node lemma and arity opening. Classical annihilating-form and coordinate methods retain their background credit. No predecessor executable is imported or run.

## Evidence

- Before: #6653 leaves arity 15 open after an integer-direction box search; #7475 supplies a different arity-24 construction. Neither is replayed here.
- After: both new full censuses visit 5,040 primitive directions and all 12,698,280 unordered pairs, rejecting every candidate. The primary method rejects 17 repeated third directions and 12,698,263 non-dyadic forced weights. The separate method transforms to the selected two source coordinates and compares mixed cubic coefficients.

CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, standard library only. Both full checkers pass normally and under `-O`, with eight primary and fourteen coordinate-check fixtures. The four timed direct commands take 16.79, 17.04, 16.28 and 16.00 seconds. Each is below its registered 300-second limit. These are replay-duration records, not a performance comparison.

The full registered runner passes in 66.18 seconds with `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=partial`. Metadata/source pins and committed-byte/source-history preflight pass for all ten package/input files. The selected source-binding orientation passes; no selected scientific replay was run.

From the repository root, exact reproduction commands are:

```sh
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/cubic-r15-height-obstruction
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/cubic-r15-height-obstruction/verify.py
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/cubic-r15-height-obstruction/independent.py
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/cubic-r15-height-obstruction --check-source-history
```

The registered command runs every `VERIFY.json` check, including both optimized runs. Expected counts are 12,698,280 pairs and zero admissible triples in every run. The written proof explains why the third row is unrestricted and why primitive normalization preserves dyadic weights.

## Limitations

This does not establish a three-query construction, a four-query lower bound, a sharp height cutoff, a physical cost saving, new kappa or supplier admission. The finite execution proves the stated bounded-pair exclusion; it does not control arbitrary coefficient heights. Native realization, chronology and restoration costs, routing, precision/storage, a complete caller invoice and the five selected framework assumptions remain outside scope. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No Lean, Docker or selected-supplier cold replay ran.

The original construction claim was narrowed to this obstruction in the [scope update](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19591562). Broader searches stopped at this first useful result.

## Open next questions

- Does arity 15 admit an exact three-query dyadic repair with at least two primitive directions above height 64? Start with larger pairs or a global valuation restriction, then supply an exact identity and legal restoring schedule.
- Can an unbounded family of primitive pairs be excluded algebraically? Start with the odd prime factors of the forced denominators. The finite certificate alone does not settle this.

## Related open work

- [#7475](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7475) constructs an exact three-query repair at arity 24; this contribution gives a coefficient-height obstruction at arity 15.
- [#7478](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7478) classifies one equal-weight family by a Pell recurrence; this contribution allows every dyadic weight within its bounded-pair domain.
- [#7479](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7479) proves three-query solvability modulo every odd integer; this contribution restricts one exact global dyadic representation and does not assert modular nonexistence.

The completion check read this account's other seven open PRs created since the CLAIM: #7501, #7502, #7503, #7504, #7505, #7507 and #7509. Their scopes are physical phase/egress sharing, column-plane parity cores, tensor phase observations, canonical rotation routing, banded inverse preparation, acyclic interaction errors and quadratic phase streaming. None studies this cubic-reader repair or reports a competing coefficient-height bound. No extra mathematical computations were run to compare them.

## CI notes

**CI did not certify this package.** At unchanged head `1c839f7c793ad5070b79be2df6eacf2d6d3250ab`, [run 43437583412](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43437583412), [plan job 131926559401](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43437583412/job/131926559401), failed in `Onboarding helper tests`. I read the checks once and confirmed the actual job log. It ran 760 tests with exactly one failure and 24 skipped. The failing test was `test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`, at `tests/test_research_current_status.py:58`, with ``AssertionError: '`make frontier7000-verify`' not found`` in the CI verification document. The [package replay job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43437583412/job/131928927076) was skipped after planning failed. No hosted package replay ran.

The canonical base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57` Git objects confirm the cause: `certificates/selected-result.json` names `make frontier7000-verify`, while the current section of `docs/ci-verification.md` still describes #6030 and `make frontier6030-verify`. The test requires the selected reproduction command in that section. These shared files and the test are unchanged by this PR, whose diff contains only the seven new package files.

I also read the actual failed-job logs for rohanarun's [run 42905094314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314) and petalas's [run 43437279341](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43437279341). Both report the same sole failed test and missing-command assertion, with 760 tests and 24 skips. Run metadata confirms the fork owners. Earlier, I verified the same final test failure in apoursh's planning logs for [#7475, run 43291062509](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43291062509/job/131437108801) and [#7478, run 43291772301](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43291772301/job/131439552156). This is evidence of the shared repository-level CI blocker, not mathematical coverage for this package.

All package evidence above remains local: both complete censuses normally and under optimization, registered replay, metadata/source pins, and committed-byte/source-history checks passed at the unchanged head. No fix, retrigger commit, push, job rerun or shared-file edit was made in response to this failure. Maintainers will repair main.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: the isolated new research package and its opt-in replay. The selected frontier and predecessor packages are unchanged.
